identity.name: Delta-tocopherol
identity.chemical_class: Tocopherol (vitamin E isoform; lipophilic phenolic antioxidant)

function.mechanism: Chain-breaking antioxidant in lipid phases that interrupts propagation of oxidative radical reactions and slows rancidity.
common_food_categories: foods using tocopherols under GMP antioxidant use

adi.basis: EFSA 2015 E306-E309 re-evaluation concluded no need for a numerical ADI for tocopherols as food additives; EFSA also referenced a historical group ADI context of 2 mg/kg bw/day for vitamin E source use.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded tocopherols (including E309) were not of safety concern at reported food-additive uses/use levels.

adi.basis: No standalone delta-tocopherol/E309 record found in WHO JECFA partial-name search; closest additive entry is Mixed TOCOPHEROLS concentrate (INS 306) with ADI 0-2 mg/kg bw.

concerns.summary: A 2025 CKD cohort reported a U-shaped association between dietary delta-tocopherol and CKD progression risk, suggesting possible non-linear intake-response in a vulnerable population.
A 2026 prospective cohort associated several preservatives, including alpha-tocopherol, with higher incident type 2 diabetes; relevance to E309 specifically is indirect and observational.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2015 re-evaluation for E306-E309 concluded no safety concern at reported additive uses/use levels.
Short-term phase-0 supplementation with a tocopherol mixture that increased delta-tocopherol tissue levels reported no adverse events.
No IARC monograph classification entry was identified for delta-tocopherol in the IARC list dataset reviewed.

populations: high-end consumers of tocopherols from all dietary sources
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA indexed metadata for the 2015 opinion reported high-percentile total-source tocopherol exposure up to 8.49 mg/kg bw/day, above the older 2 mg/kg bw/day vitamin E-source ADI context; additive-specific exceedance for E309 alone remains uncertain.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory bodies currently support tocopherol use (EFSA no-safety-concern conclusion for additive use; FDA GRAS/GMP), and no IARC carcinogenic classification or major ban signal was identified. Remaining uncertainty comes from limited E309-specific modern exposure granularity and observational non-linear associations in CKD populations.
key_factors: EFSA 2015 E306-E309 re-evaluation reported no safety concern for additive use
No numerical additive ADI set by EFSA for tocopherols in that opinion
FDA eCFR lists tocopherols under GRAS with GMP conditions (21 CFR 182.3890 and 182.1)
No standalone JECFA delta-tocopherol record identified; closest INS 306 mixed tocopherols ADI is 0-2 mg/kg bw
No IARC monograph listing identified for delta-tocopherol
Recent observational CKD data suggest possible non-linear association for dietary delta-tocopherol
